routes.reason: New roadmap, 75 items and the bulk of the extraction. Accepted: nothing in the atlas plans a local Langlands correspondence for G_2, and the paper's whole architecture — the map L, its surjectivity, the description of its fibres, and the characterisation by the properties (i), (ii), (iii) and (ix) of the Main Theorem — is new ground. The name is free and no other paper proposes it.

New roadmap, 25 items. Accepted, and it is a merge rather than a fresh claim: PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23, the companion paper 'Howe duality and dichotomy for exceptional theta correspondences', proposes the same roadmap. Splitting the exceptional theta machinery out of the G_2 correspondence is right, since the two Gan–Savin papers share it and the dichotomy is used here as an input (Theorem 2.1(ii)) rather than proved. The name is free.

Part II of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, 14 items, with a title that is an exact prefix extension of its parent's and a free name. The unitary-dual topology of Appendix B is genuinely in the parent's direction and is not planned by any existing layer.

notes: Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-d67081, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by cc-442dc5. Verdict accept: no item, status, route or locator changed. All 128 items, 6 routes and 15 recorded mistakes were checked against the published open-access text, Forum Math. Pi 11 (2023), e28, 42 pp., re-fetched for this review; printed page = PDF page. All 15 recorded mistakes are confirmed, and four are settled decisively by the paper's own text. E3: the Main Theorem (ix) on p. 4 prints γ(s, std ∘ L(π)) ⊗ φ_τ, ψ), whose brackets do not balance — the close after L(π) shuts γ( prematurely. E6: p. 11 introduces a totally real field k and then takes 'a totally definite octonion algebra over F', although the next sentence speaks of G_v at all archimedean and finite places, which only a global object over k has. E13: p. 36 prints the same formula correctly as L_{Sp_6} eighteen lines before printing it as L_{Sp_6 6}. E5: Theorem 2.1's parts are (i) Howe duality and (ii) theta dichotomy, and it is (ii) that gives the decomposition of Irr(G_2), yet pp. 8 and 10 both cite (i). The two gaps are confirmed with their scope stated. E2 is the more consequential, and the paper's own Theorem 2.1(ii) is what shows a hypothesis is missing: Theorem 9.1(ii) is stated for every π ∈ Irr(G_2), but the theta dichotomy says π has nonzero lift to exactly one of PD^× or PGSp_6, so for those lifting to PD^× the phrase 'its local theta lift θ(π) ∈ Irr(PGSp_6)' has no referent. I confirm that a restriction is needed and leave its exact form — the extraction proposes φ ∈ Φ^♦_ds(G_2) — to the extraction. E1 is confirmed as printed, with the scope of its repair likewise resting on the extraction. Where a finding bundles a principal element with subsidiary ones, or where its correction depends on re-deriving an identity rather than reading the page, the verdict says so explicitly. E10 is the one I could not settle from the text layer at all — the symbol after 'parameterized by' is dropped — and I confirm it on the sentence's own logic rather than on a glyph reading, and say so. A provenance problem was found and recorded: the source block's sha256 for the published PDF is NOT reproducible, because Cambridge stamps each download. Two downloads gave two hashes, neither the recorded one, differing only in the stamp. A reproducible stamp-stripped text hash, f35be3dd…66f5, was recorded in its place; the arXiv hash the source block also carries remains a second anchor. The single library citation was read at the pinned commit and is right: item 114 cites Banach–Alaoglu, and Mathlib's isCompact_closedBall and isCompact_polar in Analysis/Normed/Module/WeakDual.lean say what the item claims. All 4 planned items name atlas layers that exist, all 123 missing items are routed exactly once, and there is no run-together numbering. Both new roadmap names are free and both Part II titles are exact prefix extensions of their parents'. ExceptionalThetaCorrespondencesForG2 is co-proposed by PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23, the companion paper, which is the right structure: the dichotomy is used here as an input rather than proved, so the two papers sharing one roadmap for it is a merge and not a duplication. Every check is listed in research/blueprint/reviews/REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23-B.md.
